name: Silhouette Try-On
need: See roughly how a garment would sit on you before you buy it — without an app, an account, or a photo upload.
description: Upload a photo of yourself and a photo of a garment (a product shot, a screenshot from a shop) and see a rough schematic overlay of where it would sit on your body: its position and width against your shoulders and hips. A MediaPipe pose model (vendored, running entirely in-browser) finds your shoulders and hips; a from-scratch flood-fill removes the garment photo's background; a from-scratch piecewise-affine warp maps the garment onto your torso and draws it as a semi-transparent, dashed-outline overlay — deliberately not photorealistic, so it never claims to show something it can't. Every current try-on tool that looks photoreal is either an app-store download, requires an account, or metes out paid credits per generation, because photoreal garment transfer needs a GPU model that costs money to run per use. This sidesteps that entirely: both photos are processed on your device and never uploaded anywhere, so there is no per-use cost and nothing to meter.
limitations: Not photorealistic. It shows a garment's rough position and width against your torso — not fabric drape, stretch, texture, or how it will actually look worn.
Only approximates the torso region between shoulders and hips. Sleeves, necklines, hems, and overall garment length are not modeled.
Needs a clear, front-facing photo with your shoulders and hips both visible. Side-on poses, heavy cropping, or poor lighting will fail to detect a pose rather than guess.

Garment cutout works by removing a plain or near-uniform background. It will not cleanly separate a garment against a busy or textured background, worn by a model, on a hanger with clutter around it, or under strong shadows.
The warp assumes the garment photo is roughly front-facing and flat (typical of a product photo). An angled or draped shot will distort more than a flat one.
Detects one person per photo and picks the most prominent one if several people are in frame.
First load downloads roughly 15–18MB of pose-detection model files. Cached by the browser after that; works offline from the second load on.
Says nothing about sizing or fit — it shows where a garment would sit, not whether it would fit.
evidence: https://www.mumsnet.com/talk/am_i_being_unreasonable/5386604-the-next-big-thing-for-online-clothes-shopping — thread on wanting real virtual try-on for online clothes shopping, noting existing versions have been basic for over a decade

https://retail-insider.com/retail-insider/2026/07/online-clothing-leads-e-commerce-returns-with-sizing-driving-most-send-backs-overnight-glasses/ — sizing drives most online-clothing returns, 2026 industry data
https://www.richpanel.com/learn/ecommerce-return-rates — apparel e-commerce return rates run 20-40%, fit and sizing the largest single cause

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/ai-virtual-try-on-clothes/id6736467247 — a representative paid competitor: $6.99-$24.99 for credit packs, evidence nobody offers a free, unmetered version because photoreal generation costs money per use
